question: For real numbers \(a\) and \(b,\) define \(a\,\$\,b=(a-b)^2.\) What is \((x-y)^2\,\$\,(y-x)^2?\)
solution:
The two inputs to the operation are equal. Indeed, \(y-x=-(x-y)\), and a number and its opposite have the same square, so
\[
(y-x)^2=(x-y)^2.
\]
The rule \(a\,\$\,b=(a-b)^2\) therefore gives
\[
(x-y)^2\,\$\,(y-x)^2
=\bigl((x-y)^2-(y-x)^2\bigr)^2
=0.
\]
This holds for every real \(x\) and \(y\). The answer is \(\boxed{0}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{A}}\).
